en.title: From public T-cell engager evidence to the next experiment
en.summary: Public PopPK and efficacy reconstruction, Bayesian CRS sensitivity, and hypothetical measurement value and sampling design.
key_findings: Using the published tarlatamab PopPK and Emax models in 5,000 virtual subjects, initial exposure matched label summaries, but steady-state troughs did not fully agree.
Bayesian models of three aggregate CRS windows fitted the data, but the exposure-history timescale depended on the prior, so no optimal step-up among 14 schedules could be chosen.

Matching dose intensity preserved average exposure but changed peaks and troughs, and early-only sampling did not stabilize CL; the framework specifies which measurements could change a decision, not a validated regimen.
